glasses_dana: Previous notes suggested coffee_table_l1 for daytime, but today at 07:44 it was at bathroom_shelf_ba1. This contradicts the "living room hub" pattern for early morning. The location is highly volatile. Check bathroom_shelf_ba1 for early morning (pre-9 AM) and nightstand_b1 for late night (post-22:00). Do not default to coffee_table_l1 for all daytime queries.

water_bottle_dana: Previous notes suggested coffee_table_l1 for afternoon, but today at 19:54 it was at kitchen_table_k1. This indicates the bottle moves to the kitchen in the evening, not just the living room. Check coffee_table_l1 for mid-day (10:00-15:00) and kitchen_table_k1 for evening (post-18:00). The "living room hub" pattern does not apply to evening hours.

mug_dana: Previous notes assumed desk_o1 during work hours, but today it was at coffee_table_l1 at 09:22 and 11:14. This contradicts the "stays at office desk" pattern. The mug appears to be in the living room during the day. Check coffee_table_l1 for daytime locations.

book_dana: Previous notes suggested bed_b1 for evening, but today at 10:52 it was at coffee_table_l1. This indicates the book is frequently in the living room during the day, not just the bedroom. Check coffee_table_l1 for daytime locations.

glass_dana: Previous notes suggested counter_k1 for afternoon, but today at 22:19 it was at nightstand_b1. This confirms the late-night location is the bedroom. Check nightstand_b1 for late night locations.

General Pattern: The "coffee_table_l1 as central hub" heuristic is too broad. It applies to mid-day (10:00-15:00) for mugs, books, and water bottles, but fails for early morning glasses (bathroom) and evening water bottles (kitchen). Time-of-day specificity is critical.
